_comment: Skia for macOS, built by this project because the one upstream publishes is
compiled for the wrong GL.
Skia's gn/skia.gni sets skia_gl_standard = "gl" when is_mac, which defines
SK_ASSUME_GL=1 and compiles the ES interface assembler out. The only GL on
Apple is ANGLE, which is ES, so every Canvas2D surface on macOS fails to
build a GrDirectContext against a prebuilt carrying that define -- silently,
because WebGL never goes through Skia and nothing else asks. The archives
here are the same sources built with skia_gl_standard="", which restores
the runtime dispatch every other platform already gets.
iOS is NOT here and must not be: its default is "gles", which is what ANGLE
actually is, so upstream's iOS prebuilts are correct and cheaper than ours.
scripts/apple-skia-gl-env.sh is sourced only on the macOS platform, which is
what keeps that true.
The recipe is scripts/package-apple-skia-binaries.sh and the machine that
runs it is .github/workflows/apple-skia-binaries.yml. Both refuse to package
a downloaded build, which is the mistake a rebuild is most likely to make.
The objects are compiled against the macOS deployment floor in
contracts/apple/deployment-floor.json, which the tag names. The first archives
(tag skia-apple-0.93.1-31932366) were not: clang took the build runner's OS, so every
Skia object said minos 15.0 against an 11.0 floor. The recipe now checks the bytes
before packaging, and a published tag is never re-uploaded.
Builds do not let skia-bindings download these. Its downloader caches by file
name and resumes, the names are upstream's, and a build directory that once held
upstream's archive linked it again with a green build. scripts/materialise-apple-skia.py
fetches them whole, checks size and sha256 against this file, and hands
skia-bindings a file:// URL.
_url_template_comment: skia-bindings expands {tag} and {key} in SKIA_BINARIES_URL. The key is its
own construction -- commit, target triple, feature set -- so one template
serves both darwin triples and a key it cannot find simply misses and
source-builds, which is slow and never wrong.
